q: How do I calculate the cold chain emissions for one kilogram of food?
title: Cold chain emissions per kg of food
short: Add each cold stage per kilogram: pre-cooling and cold storage electricity at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, reefer truck diesel at 2.68 kg per litre, and retail chilling. Get each stage's energy per kilogram from the operator, and add refrigerant leaks where they are reported.
audience: Food brands, exporters and cold chain operators

ul: Reefer transport, including the refrigeration unit's fuel.

p: Ask each operator for energy per kilogram or per pallet-day. Where you estimate, state the assumption and label it.
A good cold chain reduces spoilage, which avoids wasting the farm footprint. Note loss rates as context, without netting them against cold chain emissions.

example.title: Worked example: one kilogram of produce (illustrative inputs)
lines: Pre-cooling: 0.04 kWh per kg x 0.710 = 0.0284 kg CO2
Cold store, 20 days: 0.12 kWh per kg x 0.710 = 0.0852 kg CO2
Reefer truck: 0.03 L diesel per kg x 2.68 = 0.0804 kg CO2
Retail chiller: 0.05 kWh per kg x 0.710 = 0.0355 kg CO2
Cold chain total: 0.2295 kg CO2 per kg of food
example.note: Values are illustrative; get per-kilogram energy from each operator.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and fuel card statements (diesel 2.68 and CNG 2.69 kg CO2, IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 record. Hired transport goes to the Scope 3 evidence trail, and distance or tonne-km estimates are labelled as estimates.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard
